Here’s the complete 12-week couch-to-5K plan summary integrating run progression, interval and tempo additions, strength training, EIA-specific precautions, a Week 8 parkrun benchmark, and a finisher/race-week.

Global guidelines for exercise-induced asthma (EIA)
- Always carry inhaler; if prescribed, 2 puffs SABA 10–15 min pre-run (especially intervals/tempo/race).
- Warm-up every session (12–15 min): 5–6 min brisk walk/easy jog, dynamic mobility (ankles/hips/T-spine), 3–4 x 20–30s strides RPE 5–6 with 60–90s walk. Keep first 5–10 min of the main run very easy.
- Prefer warm/humid air; in cold/dry air wear a buff/heat-moisture exchanger and extend warm-up by 3–5 min. Consider treadmill when cold.
- Cool-down 8–10 min easy walk/jog + gentle breathing/mobility.
- Intensity by RPE: Easy 3–4, Steady 5, Tempo/Threshold 6–7, Strides 6 (20–30s only).
- Progression rule: If symptoms or undue fatigue occur, repeat or regress the week.

Weekly layout template
- 3 run days/week: one quality (intervals from Week 6), one tempo (from Week 8), one long easy.
- 2 strength days/week (lighter on heavy run weeks).
- Spacing example: Mon easy+strength, Wed intervals, Fri tempo, Sun long easy. Adjust to schedule with ≥48 h between hard runs.

Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–3)
Goal: Build consistent walk-jog, perfect warm-up/cool-down, practice breath control.

Week 1
- Runs (3x):
  - A: 8 x 1 min jog (RPE 3) / 90s walk
  - B: 9 x 1 min jog / 90s walk
  - C: 10 x 1 min jog / 90s walk
- Strength (2x, 20–25 min): Squat 3x8–10, DB RDL 3x8, split squat 2x8/side, step-up 2x8/side, calf raises 3x12–15, side plank 3x20–30s/side, dead bug 3x6–8/side, ankle/T-spine mobility.

Week 2
- Runs:
  - A: 6 x 90s jog / 2 min walk
  - B: 7 x 90s jog / 2 min walk
  - C: 8 x 90s jog / 2 min walk
- Strength: Same as Week 1; progress slightly.

Week 3
- Runs:
  - A: 5 x 2 min jog / 2 min walk
  - B: 6 x 2 min jog / 2 min walk
  - C: 7 x 2 min jog / 90s walk
- Strength: Add single-leg RDL 2x8/side; continue core and calf work.

Phase 2: Build continuous time (Weeks 4–6)
Goal: Extend run intervals toward continuous running; introduce intervals in Week 6.

Week 4
- Runs:
  - A: 5 x 3 min jog / 90s walk
  - B: 4 x 4 min jog / 2 min walk
  - C: 3 x 6 min jog / 2 min walk
- Strength (2x, 25–35 min): Goblet squat 3x6–8, DB RDL 3x8, step-ups 2–3x8/side, calf raises 3x12–15, plank 3x30–45s, bird-dog 3x6/side, band walks 2x12–15.

Week 5
- Runs:
  - A: 4 x 6 min jog / 90s walk
  - B: 3 x 8 min jog / 2 min walk
  - C: 2 x 10 min jog / 3 min walk
- Optional post-run: 4 x 20s relaxed strides if lungs feel good.
- Strength: Maintain; progress load modestly.

Week 6
- Runs:
  - A: 12 min jog / 3 min walk / 8 min jog
  - B: Intervals (replace midweek run): 8 x 1 min steady (RPE 5) / 2 min easy jog
  - C: 18 min jog / 2 min walk / 8 min jog
- Strength: KB deadlift/box squat variants appear; keep total 2x/week, 25–35 min.

Phase 3: Transition to continuous + add intensity safely (Weeks 7–9)
Week 7
- Runs:
  - A: 20 min continuous easy
  - B: Intervals: 6 x 90s steady (RPE 5) / 2 min easy
  - C: 25 min continuous easy
- Strength: Lighter deload (3x6 main lifts; brief accessory).

Week 8
- Runs with parkrun benchmark:
  - Early week easy: 25–30 min easy (or short fartlek if skipping intervals)
  - Midweek Intervals: 5 x 2 min RPE 5–6 / 2 min easy (optional reduce to 4 reps for freshness)
  - Saturday: Parkrun 5K at controlled effort cap RPE ~6. Use full EIA warm-up. First km RPE 4–5, settle 5–6, finish smooth. Cool-down 8–10 min.
  - Sunday: 25–30 min very easy or rest
- Strength: Earlier in week only; skip heavy work within 24 h pre-parkrun.
- Tempo: Parkrun replaces this week’s tempo.

Week 9
- Runs (add controlled pace work):
  - A: 30 min easy + 4 x 20s strides
  - B: Intervals: 6 x 2 min RPE 5–6 / 90s easy
  - C: 32 min easy; last 5 min at RPE 4–5 if comfortable
- Optional: Aerobic fartlek alternative for B if outdoors conditions poor.

Phase 4: From 30 min to 5K, sharpen gradually (Weeks 10–12)
Week 10
- Runs:
  - A: Intervals: 5 x 3 min at threshold feel (RPE 6–7) / 2 min easy
  - B: Tempo: 15–18 min continuous at RPE 6–7 (or 2 x 8–9 min with 2 min easy if cold/dry)
  - C: 34–36 min easy continuous
- Strength: Keep but avoid heavy lifting ≤24 h before A or B.

Week 11
- Runs:
  - A: Cruise intervals: 3 x 5 min at RPE 6–7 / 3 min easy
  - B: Tempo with finish pickup: 12 min at RPE 6 → 3 min easy → 6 min RPE 6–7
  - C: Broken 5K rhythm: 2 km easy → 3 x 800 m at 5K feel (RPE 6–7) with 400 m easy → 5–8 min easy
- Strength: Light-moderate; reduce volume ~20–30%.

Week 12: Finisher/Race-week prep
- Mon: Off or 20 min easy + mobility/core
- Tue (Sharpening): 3 x 3 min steady (RPE 5) / 2 min easy + strides in warm-up; total ≤35–40 min
- Thu (Tempo primer): 2 x 6–8 min at RPE 5–6 / 3 min easy; stop fresh
- Fri: Off or 15 min very easy + 4 x 15s relaxed strides
- Sun (Race day 5K):
  - Warm-up: 6–8 min walk/jog → dynamic mobility → 3–4 x 20–30s strides (60–90s walk)
  - Pacing: Km1 RPE 4–5; Km2–4 RPE 5–6; Km5 upper RPE 6 if lungs clear. No surging.
  - Cool-down: 10 min easy walk/jog; breathing/mobility 2–3 min
- Strength: One very light session early week only (bodyweight split squat 2x8/side, hip bridge 2x10, calf raise 2x10, side plank 2x20–25s/side)

Strength training summary (2x/week unless noted)
- Weeks 1–3 (Foundation): Goblet squat, DB RDL, split squat/step-up, calf raises (incl. eccentric), glute bridge/hip thrust, single-arm row, Pallof press, core (side plank, dead bug), ankle/T-spine mobility.
- Weeks 4–6 (Build): Slightly heavier loads; RFESS, step-downs, band work; maintain calf/soleus focus.
- Week 7 (Deload): Reduce sets 20–30%.
- Weeks 8–11 (Maintain + low-impact plyo): Box squat/KB deadlift moderate sets; add light pogo/skipping and running drills (A-march/skip) if symptom-free; keep 48–72 h from long run; skip plyo if any calf/Achilles niggle.
- Week 12 (Taper): Very light, early in week only.

Nutrition, recovery, and monitoring
- Sleep 7–9 h; hydrate 2–3 L/day; don’t neglect fluids in cold weather.
- Pre-run: Light carb-focused snack 60–120 min before (e.g., fruit + yogurt).
- Post-run: 20–30 g protein + carbs within 1–2 h.
- Illness/allergy/cold-dry flare: Favor treadmill, reduce intensity, or rest.
- Soreness/pain rule: Joint pain >3/10 or EIA symptoms lingering post-cool-down → hold progression; repeat/reduce the week.

Pace guidance using the Week 8 parkrun
- Easy ≈ parkrun pace + 60–90 sec/km
- Steady ≈ parkrun pace + 30–45 sec/km
- Tempo ≈ parkrun pace + 15–30 sec/km
- Strides: fast-relaxed for 20–30s, never all-out

This integrated 12-week plan builds him from couch to a confident, asthma-smart 5K with progressive volume, carefully staged intensity (intervals and tempo), robust strength work, a Week 8 benchmark, and a race-prep finisher week. Adjust week-to-week based on symptoms, sleep, and weather to keep progress safe and consistent.

- Strength and mobility: 2 short sessions/week to support running economy and reduce injury risk.
- Progression safety: If any week feels too hard or triggers symptoms, repeat that week before moving on.

- Warm‑up and cool‑down are listed each time

- Session B: 15 min jog / 3 min walk / 10 min jog.
- Session C: 18 min jog / 2 min walk / 8 min jog.

- Session B: 22 min continuous jog.
- Session C: 25 min continuous jog.
- Strength (1–2x): Keep light—focus on form, not fatigue.

- Session B: 25 min continuous jog.
- Session C: 28 min continuous jog.

- Session B: 20 min easy jog.
- Session C: 32 min continuous jog.
- Strength: Single‑leg focus—step‑downs 2x8/side, glute bridge 3x10, side plank 3x30s/side.

Phase 4: From 30 minutes to 5K (Weeks 10–12)
Goals: Consolidate continuous running, gently extend duration or add controlled pickups, complete a comfortable 5K.

Week 10
- Session A: 30 min easy jog (RPE 3).
- Session B: Aerobic fartlek: 5 x 2 min “steady” (RPE 5, still nose–mouth comfortable) with 2 min easy jog between. Total 30–34 min including recoveries.
- Session C: 34–36 min easy continuous jog.
- Note: Pickups are modest; avoid sharp surges to reduce bronchospasm risk.

Week 11
- Session A: 32–34 min easy jog.
- Session B: Progressive easy run: 10 min very easy → 15 min easy → 5–7 min steady (RPE 4–5). Total ~32 min.
- Session C: Practice 5K on flat route or track at comfortable effort; if symptoms appear, slow to easy pace or insert 1–2 min walk breaks.

Week 12 (Taper into 5K event/benchmark)
- Session A: 25 min easy jog + 4 x 20s relaxed strides with full 80–90s walk recoveries.
- Session B: 20 min very easy jog; focus on warm‑up routine and breathing.
- Session C: 5K day
  - Extended warm‑up: 6–8 min brisk walk, dynamic drills, 3 x 20s light jog strides with 60–90s walk.
  - Start conservatively (first 1–2 km at RPE 3–4). If feeling good and lungs stable, gradually nudge to RPE 4–5 in final 1–2 km.
  - Cool‑down: 10 min easy walk; hydration; 5–10 min relaxed mobility.

Breathing, warm‑up, and cold‑air protocol (use every session)
- Step 1: Environment check: Prefer temps >5–8°C; if colder, wear buff over mouth/nose, extend warm‑up by 3–5 min, favor nasal breathing early to humidify air.
- Step 2: Medication: If advised by GP/asthma plan, take SABA 10–15 min pre‑run. Carry inhaler and ID.
- Step 3: Warm‑up (12–15 min)
  - 5 min brisk walk.
  - Dynamic mobility: ankle circles, leg swings front/side, hip openers, thoracic rotations (30–45s each).
  - 3–4 x 20–30s easy strides or light jog pick‑ups with 60–90s walk. Keep effort submaximal (RPE 5 at most).
- Step 4: First 5–10 min of main set: Keep pace very easy; avoid rapid hills.
- Step 5: Cool‑down: 8–10 min easy walk; box breathing 4–6 cycles; gentle stretches.

Recovery and monitoring
- Sleep: Aim 7–9 hours. Poor sleep day? Keep the session easy or swap rest.
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day; pre‑run 300–500 mL water; in cold, don’t neglect fluids.
- Nutrition: Balanced meals; include carbs around sessions (e.g., fruit + yogurt 60–90 min pre‑run; recovery snack with 20–30 g protein + carbs within 1–2 h).
- Illness/allergy days: Reduce to walk‑only or rest. Pollen/cold, dry winds can aggravate—use buff, choose indoor treadmill if available.
- Soreness scale: If joint pain >3/10 or asthma symptoms linger after cool‑down, repeat or regress the week.

Contingencies
- If cold‑air symptoms appear despite precautions: Move key sessions indoors (treadmill) for that week; reduce any “steady” pickups; resume progression when stable for 7 consecutive days.
- If a week is missed: Repeat the last successfully completed week rather than jumping ahead.

By Week 12, he should comfortably complete 5K at an easy, sustainable effort with minimized EIA risk, strong warm‑up habits, and a foundation for further 5K performance training if desired.

How to structure Week 8 with a parkrun test
- Goal: Comfortable benchmark and practice of warm‑up, pacing, and recovery. Effort cap = RPE 6 (comfortably hard), not a max.
- Weekly flow example:
  - Mon: Easy run 25–30 min + light mobility/core
  - Wed: Intervals (Week 8 prescription: 5 x 2 min at RPE 5–6, 2 min easy) OR swap to a lighter fartlek if you want extra freshness
  - Fri: OFF or 20 min easy + 4 x 20s relaxed strides
  - Sat: Parkrun test (see below)
  - Sun: 25–30 min very easy shake‑out or rest, depending on how he feels

Parkrun day plan (Week 8, Saturday)
- Pre‑run
  - Environment check: If cold/dry, prefer treadmill another week; otherwise wear a buff/heat‑moisture exchanger and extend warm‑up 3–5 min.
  - Medication: If prescribed/approved, 2 puffs SABA 10–15 minutes pre‑start. Carry inhaler and ID.
  - Warm‑up (12–15 min):
    - 6 min brisk walk/easy jog
    - Dynamic mobility: ankles, hips, T‑spine (30–45s each)
    - 3 x 20–30s relaxed strides at RPE 5–6 with 60–90s walk
    - First 5 minutes post‑start: run at very easy RPE 3–4 to settle breathing.
- Pacing strategy
  - Km 1: RPE 4–5. Hold back; focus on smooth, controlled breathing.
  - Km 2–4: Settle at RPE 5–6 (comfortably hard, short phrases possible).
  - Km 5: If lungs feel clear and controlled, nudge to upper RPE 6; avoid surging.
  - If coughing/wheezing/tightness persists beyond mild after easing for 1–2 minutes, down‑shift to easy jog/walk and finish comfortably—data still counts.
- Cool‑down
  - 8–10 min easy walk/jog
  - Gentle mobility + diaphragmatic/box breathing 2–3 minutes
  - Hydrate; have a carb‑protein snack within 60 minutes

How to use the result
- Record: total time, average RPE per km, any symptom notes (onset, triggers, recovery), and weather.
- Derive training paces:
  - Easy pace ≈ parkrun pace + 60–90 sec/km
  - Steady pace ≈ parkrun pace + 30–45 sec/km
  - Tempo pace ≈ parkrun pace + 15–30 sec/km
  - These are starting points; always prioritize RPE and symptom control.
- If the test felt too easy (RPE ≤5 throughout, no symptoms), you can:
  - Add 1 rep to the next week’s interval set or extend each rep by 30 seconds, or
  - Add 2–3 minutes to the Week 9 long easy run.
- If symptoms cropped up or RPE spiked early, keep Week 9 the same as Week 8 or reduce intensity (steady instead of threshold) and prioritize indoor sessions if cold/dry.

Adjusting nearby sessions
- Intervals in Week 8: Keep as prescribed or reduce to 4 x 2 min (RPE 5–6) for extra freshness.
- Tempo in Week 8: Replace the scheduled tempo workout with the parkrun. The effort cap (RPE 6) makes it a safe stand‑in.
- Strength: Keep lower‑body strength earlier in the week (Tue) and upper/light core on Thu. Skip heavy lifting within 24 hours before parkrun.

Contingencies
- Cold/dry morning or pollen spike: Move the “test” to a treadmill 5K time trial with identical warm‑up and pacing. Or run parkrun easy and keep the test for Week 9.
- If he’s ill or has exacerbations that week: Do not test. Swap for 25–30 min easy jog, and resume progression when symptom‑free per his asthma action plan.

This keeps Week 8 focused, gives a realistic benchmark, and reinforces his EIA‑friendly race routine without compromising the build to Week 12.

Here’s a dedicated finisher/race‑day prep week you can place as Week 12 (or slide to Week 13 if you keep Week 12 as a heavier training week). It sharpens without fatigue, rehearses EIA‑specific routines, and builds confidence for a smooth 5K.

Overview
- Objectives: Freshen legs, stabilize breathing, polish pacing, finalize logistics.
- Structure: 2 short quality touches + 1 easy primer + race day.
- Effort cap: Nothing above RPE 6; stop any faster work at the first sign of persistent tightness/coughing.

Weekly layout (Mon–Sun example)
- Mon: Off or 20 min very easy + mobility/core 10–12 min
- Tue: Sharpening session (strides + short steady blocks)
- Wed: Off or 20 min easy + 5–8 min mobility/breathing
- Thu: Tempo primer (short, controlled)
- Fri: Off or 15 min very easy + 4 x 15s fast‑relaxed strides
- Sat: Race‑day prep (logistics, kit check, nutrition)
- Sun: 5K event

Session details
- Tuesday: Sharpening
  - Warm‑up: 5–6 min easy jog, dynamic mobility (ankles/hips/T‑spine), 3 x 20–25s strides (60–90s walk).
  - Main: 3 x 3 min steady (RPE 5) with 2 min easy jog between.
  - Cool‑down: 8–10 min easy + gentle mobility.
  - Note: Indoors if cold/dry; keep breathing smooth.

- Thursday: Tempo primer
  - Warm‑up as above.
  - Main: 2 x 6–8 min at steady–tempo (RPE 5–6) with 3 min easy jog.
  - Cool‑down: 8–10 min easy.
  - Adjust: If legs feel heavy or any EIA hints, switch to 15–20 min continuous easy.

- Friday: Neuromuscular touch (optional)
  - 15 min very easy + 4 x 15s relaxed strides, 60–90s walk/jog.
  - Skip this if there’s any lingering tightness or if cold/dry outdoors.

Race‑week warm‑up protocol (use Tue/Thu and race day)
- Environment check: Prefer mild/warm. If cold/dry, wear a buff/heat‑moisture exchanger; consider moving the short quality indoors.
- Medication: If prescribed, 2 puffs SABA 10–15 min pre‑run. Carry inhaler and ID.
- Sequence (12–15 min):
  - 5–6 min brisk walk/easy jog
  - Dynamic mobility: ankle circles, knee‑to‑wall drills, hip openers, T‑spine rotations (30–45s each)
  - 3–4 x 20–30s strides at RPE 5–6 with 60–90s walk
  - First 5 min of the run at very easy RPE 3–4

Race‑day plan (Sunday)
- Pre‑race
  - Wake‑up: Hydrate; light breakfast 2–3 h pre‑start (e.g., toast + peanut butter + banana or yogurt + granola + fruit).
  - Weather: If cold/dry, keep buff on during first km; extend warm‑up 3–5 min.
  - Medication: Follow asthma action plan; SABA 10–15 min pre‑start if prescribed.
  - Warm‑up: 6–8 min brisk walk/easy jog → dynamic mobility → 3 x 20–30s relaxed strides with 60–90s walk.
- Pacing
  - Km 1: RPE 4–5 (hold back, settle breathing).
  - Km 2–4: RPE 5–6 (comfortably hard, short phrases).
  - Km 5: If lungs feel clear, nudge to upper RPE 6; no late surges that spike ventilation.
  - If persistent symptoms despite easing for 1–2 min: jog/walk to finish—health first.
- Cool‑down
  - 8–10 min easy walk/jog; box/diaphragmatic breathing 2–3 min; gentle mobility.

Logistics and kit checklist (do on Saturday)
- Shoes you trained in; socks; layers; buff/face covering for cold/dry; hat/gloves as needed.
- Inhaler, ID/medical info, phone.
- Pin bib the night before; know the course and start corral.
- Set alarms, route to venue, bathroom plan.
- Pack simple carbs for pre/post (banana, bar) and water bottle.

Recovery plan post‑race
- Within 60–90 min: 20–30 g protein + carbs; hydrate.
- Same day: 10–15 min easy walk later if stiff.
- 24–48 h: Light mobility; optional 20–25 min easy jog when legs feel normal; resume regular training mid‑week.

Adjustments for different schedules
- If race is Saturday, shift everything one day earlier and make Friday the short easy + optional strides day.
- If he feels unusually fatigued or has EIA flare during the week, remove Thursday’s tempo primer and keep only Tuesday’s brief steady work.

This finisher week keeps him fresh, reinforces EIA‑specific routines, and delivers a confident, well‑paced 5K without compromising respiratory control.

Here’s the complete 12-week couch-to-5K plan summary integrating run progression, interval and tempo additions, strength training, EIA-specific precautions, a Week 8 parkrun benchmark, and a finisher/race-week.

Global guidelines for exercise-induced asthma (EIA)
- Always carry inhaler; if prescribed, 2 puffs SABA 10–15 min pre-run (especially intervals/tempo/race).
- Warm-up every session (12–15 min): 5–6 min brisk walk/easy jog, dynamic mobility (ankles/hips/T-spine), 3–4 x 20–30s strides RPE 5–6 with 60–90s walk. Keep first 5–10 min of the main run very easy.
- Prefer warm/humid air; in cold/dry air wear a buff/heat-moisture exchanger and extend warm-up by 3–5 min. Consider treadmill when cold.
- Cool-down 8–10 min easy walk/jog + gentle breathing/mobility.
- Intensity by RPE: Easy 3–4, Steady 5, Tempo/Threshold 6–7, Strides 6 (20–30s only).
- Progression rule: If symptoms or undue fatigue occur, repeat or regress the week.

Weekly layout template
- 3 run days/week: one quality (intervals from Week 6), one tempo (from Week 8), one long easy.
- 2 strength days/week (lighter on heavy run weeks).
- Spacing example: Mon easy+strength, Wed intervals, Fri tempo, Sun long easy. Adjust to schedule with ≥48 h between hard runs.

Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–3)
Goal: Build consistent walk-jog, perfect warm-up/cool-down, practice breath control.

Week 1
- Runs (3x):
  - A: 8 x 1 min jog (RPE 3) / 90s walk
  - B: 9 x 1 min jog / 90s walk
  - C: 10 x 1 min jog / 90s walk
- Strength (2x, 20–25 min): Squat 3x8–10, DB RDL 3x8, split squat 2x8/side, step-up 2x8/side, calf raises 3x12–15, side plank 3x20–30s/side, dead bug 3x6–8/side, ankle/T-spine mobility.

Week 2
- Runs:
  - A: 6 x 90s jog / 2 min walk
  - B: 7 x 90s jog / 2 min walk
  - C: 8 x 90s jog / 2 min walk
- Strength: Same as Week 1; progress slightly.

Week 3
- Runs:
  - A: 5 x 2 min jog / 2 min walk
  - B: 6 x 2 min jog / 2 min walk
  - C: 7 x 2 min jog / 90s walk
- Strength: Add single-leg RDL 2x8/side; continue core and calf work.

Phase 2: Build continuous time (Weeks 4–6)
Goal: Extend run intervals toward continuous running; introduce intervals in Week 6.

Week 4
- Runs:
  - A: 5 x 3 min jog / 90s walk
  - B: 4 x 4 min jog / 2 min walk
  - C: 3 x 6 min jog / 2 min walk
- Strength (2x, 25–35 min): Goblet squat 3x6–8, DB RDL 3x8, step-ups 2–3x8/side, calf raises 3x12–15, plank 3x30–45s, bird-dog 3x6/side, band walks 2x12–15.

Week 5
- Runs:
  - A: 4 x 6 min jog / 90s walk
  - B: 3 x 8 min jog / 2 min walk
  - C: 2 x 10 min jog / 3 min walk
- Optional post-run: 4 x 20s relaxed strides if lungs feel good.
- Strength: Maintain; progress load modestly.

Week 6
- Runs:
  - A: 12 min jog / 3 min walk / 8 min jog
  - B: Intervals (replace midweek run): 8 x 1 min steady (RPE 5) / 2 min easy jog
  - C: 18 min jog / 2 min walk / 8 min jog
- Strength: KB deadlift/box squat variants appear; keep total 2x/week, 25–35 min.

Phase 3: Transition to continuous + add intensity safely (Weeks 7–9)
Week 7
- Runs:
  - A: 20 min continuous easy
  - B: Intervals: 6 x 90s steady (RPE 5) / 2 min easy
  - C: 25 min continuous easy
- Strength: Lighter deload (3x6 main lifts; brief accessory).

Week 8
- Runs with parkrun benchmark:
  - Early week easy: 25–30 min easy (or short fartlek if skipping intervals)
  - Midweek Intervals: 5 x 2 min RPE 5–6 / 2 min easy (optional reduce to 4 reps for freshness)
  - Saturday: Parkrun 5K at controlled effort cap RPE ~6. Use full EIA warm-up. First km RPE 4–5, settle 5–6, finish smooth. Cool-down 8–10 min.
  - Sunday: 25–30 min very easy or rest
- Strength: Earlier in week only; skip heavy work within 24 h pre-parkrun.
- Tempo: Parkrun replaces this week’s tempo.

Week 9
- Runs (add controlled pace work):
  - A: 30 min easy + 4 x 20s strides
  - B: Intervals: 6 x 2 min RPE 5–6 / 90s easy
  - C: 32 min easy; last 5 min at RPE 4–5 if comfortable
- Optional: Aerobic fartlek alternative for B if outdoors conditions poor.

Phase 4: From 30 min to 5K, sharpen gradually (Weeks 10–12)
Week 10
- Runs:
  - A: Intervals: 5 x 3 min at threshold feel (RPE 6–7) / 2 min easy
  - B: Tempo: 15–18 min continuous at RPE 6–7 (or 2 x 8–9 min with 2 min easy if cold/dry)
  - C: 34–36 min easy continuous
- Strength: Keep but avoid heavy lifting ≤24 h before A or B.

Week 11
- Runs:
  - A: Cruise intervals: 3 x 5 min at RPE 6–7 / 3 min easy
  - B: Tempo with finish pickup: 12 min at RPE 6 → 3 min easy → 6 min RPE 6–7
  - C: Broken 5K rhythm: 2 km easy → 3 x 800 m at 5K feel (RPE 6–7) with 400 m easy → 5–8 min easy
- Strength: Light-moderate; reduce volume ~20–30%.

Week 12: Finisher/Race-week prep
- Mon: Off or 20 min easy + mobility/core
- Tue (Sharpening): 3 x 3 min steady (RPE 5) / 2 min easy + strides in warm-up; total ≤35–40 min
- Thu (Tempo primer): 2 x 6–8 min at RPE 5–6 / 3 min easy; stop fresh
- Fri: Off or 15 min very easy + 4 x 15s relaxed strides
- Sun (Race day 5K):
  - Warm-up: 6–8 min walk/jog → dynamic mobility → 3–4 x 20–30s strides (60–90s walk)
  - Pacing: Km1 RPE 4–5; Km2–4 RPE 5–6; Km5 upper RPE 6 if lungs clear. No surging.
  - Cool-down: 10 min easy walk/jog; breathing/mobility 2–3 min
- Strength: One very light session early week only (bodyweight split squat 2x8/side, hip bridge 2x10, calf raise 2x10, side plank 2x20–25s/side)

Strength training summary (2x/week unless noted)
- Weeks 1–3 (Foundation): Goblet squat, DB RDL, split squat/step-up, calf raises (incl. eccentric), glute bridge/hip thrust, single-arm row, Pallof press, core (side plank, dead bug), ankle/T-spine mobility.
- Weeks 4–6 (Build): Slightly heavier loads; RFESS, step-downs, band work; maintain calf/soleus focus.
- Week 7 (Deload): Reduce sets 20–30%.
- Weeks 8–11 (Maintain + low-impact plyo): Box squat/KB deadlift moderate sets; add light pogo/skipping and running drills (A-march/skip) if symptom-free; keep 48–72 h from long run; skip plyo if any calf/Achilles niggle.
- Week 12 (Taper): Very light, early in week only.

Nutrition, recovery, and monitoring
- Sleep 7–9 h; hydrate 2–3 L/day; don’t neglect fluids in cold weather.
- Pre-run: Light carb-focused snack 60–120 min before (e.g., fruit + yogurt).
- Post-run: 20–30 g protein + carbs within 1–2 h.
- Illness/allergy/cold-dry flare: Favor treadmill, reduce intensity, or rest.
- Soreness/pain rule: Joint pain >3/10 or EIA symptoms lingering post-cool-down → hold progression; repeat/reduce the week.

Pace guidance using the Week 8 parkrun
- Easy ≈ parkrun pace + 60–90 sec/km
- Steady ≈ parkrun pace + 30–45 sec/km
- Tempo ≈ parkrun pace + 15–30 sec/km
- Strides: fast-relaxed for 20–30s, never all-out

This integrated 12-week plan builds him from couch to a confident, asthma-smart 5K with progressive volume, carefully staged intensity (intervals and tempo), robust strength work, a Week 8 benchmark, and a race-prep finisher week. Adjust week-to-week based on symptoms, sleep, and weather to keep progress safe and consistent.
